_comment_username: Your Whatnot username, exactly as it appears. When a giveaway is drawn the stream shows '<name> won the giveaway!' — this is what that gets compared against. Leave it blank and wins are only noticed later, from the purchases tab.
_comment_accounts: Switchable Whatnot accounts, one active at a time (active_account = index below). Each has its own Chrome profile = its own login, so switching profile switches account. The domestic-only filter reads each account's own country from its Apollo cache automatically, so a GB account sees UK sellers as domestic (joinable). my_username above stays as a fallback for the first account.
_comment_mute: Six streams at once is unbearable otherwise. Measured safe: --mute-audio is applied in Chrome's audio pipeline and is invisible to the page — video.muted, volume and AudioContext.state are all unchanged.
_comment_expand: Leave this false — and it can stay off for good now. Prize, entry rule (followers/buyers/domestic-only), your own eligibility, AND the winner are all read passively from the tab's own WebSocket frames (added 2026-08-13). Nothing left that clicking would surface. Kept only because a future Whatnot change could break the socket reading; if that ever happens, see SPEC.md before turning this on — Whatnot runs Kasada and ships a bot-detection field literally named playwright_bot, and ~70 unprompted clicks an hour is a pattern.
_comment_confirm: How many consecutive polls a giveaway must be visible before alerting. 2 rides out a half-rendered frame without costing real time.
_comment_silence: Warn if no tab has matched anything for this long — the silent failure of this design is Whatnot changing their markup.
_comment_foreign_domestic: How to treat a domestic-only giveaway from a seller in another country — one you cannot enter at all. "shadow" (default) changes nothing: it logs WOULD HAVE STAYED QUIET and adds the seller's country to the push, so the call can be checked before it is trusted. "mute" actually silences those. "off" ignores the whole thing. The seller's country is read from the page's own Apollo cache (ListingNode.shippingDetails, absent only when the seller is in your country); the domestic-only flag comes from the socket. Anything unknown is announced.
_comment_presence: A live stream sends view-count and reaction frames every few seconds, so a tab that has been silent this many seconds has almost certainly lost its socket — meaning you have quietly fallen out of that stream and stopped counting as a viewer for its giveaways. When that happens the watcher pushes you to reload the tab; it never reloads it itself. Set 0 to disable.
_comment_purchases_poll: How often (seconds) the purchases tab's own Apollo query is asked to refetch itself. Added 2026-08-13: that page never refreshes on its own — confirmed by hand — so a real win could sit unseen forever otherwise. This is one real network request, the same one a manual reload makes, so it is throttled well below anything pattern-like; 60s reads as an ordinary glance back at an open tab, not a bot.
_comment_close_ended: Close a stream tab automatically when the streamer ends their show (socket livestream_update status ENDED). Off by default: this is the one thing that touches a tab you opened, but it only ever closes a stream that is genuinely over.
_comment_close_dupes: Close duplicate tabs of the same stream (same /live/ UUID), keeping one. A raid or an accidental second open otherwise leaves 2-3 tabs on one stream. Off by default: it closes tabs you opened.
_comment_watchdog: If the poll loop freezes this many seconds (a wedged tab or a degraded Chrome debug port), the watcher auto-restarts itself and pushes a notice. Min 60.
_comment_restart_chrome: If the watcher cannot reach Chrome after several tries (debug port truly wedged, usually from RAM/tab overload), restart Chrome itself. The fresh Chrome opens with only its one blank tab - your old streams are NOT reopened, on purpose, since that reload is what overloads it. Off by default; it closes your tabs.
